detailed_results.text: I farm 500 ha with $40,000 cash and an $80,000 credit line in Iowa. What is my peak credit borrowing?
detailed_results.reply: With $40k cash the 500 ha cannot be fully planted. The NPV-max plan is all soybean ~138-140 ha, which uses the credit line to the limit. Peak outstanding balance is the full $80,000 line just before soybean harvest in f12 (Oct 2026). If you count cost-before-sale the feasible max is ~138 ha with peak $80,000 after the f12 cost.

detailed_results.text: With 500 ha and $50,000 cash in Iowa, what is the shadow price of additional capital?
detailed_results.reply: Optimal is soybean only at credit limit. ~172 ha feasible (50% rotation 250 ha not binding). Peak debt ~100k in f12 before harvest. You must sell ~265 t in Oct 2026 to clear debt and store ~440 t in 1000 t silo to Jun 2027 (price gain 375.76->404.09 covers 2 $/mo + interest). NPV ~162k. dNPV/dOwnK ~1.78, so value minus deposit = ~0.78 per $. Value of credit line dNPV/dL ~0.73 per $.

detailed_results.text: On 600 ha in Iowa with $60,000 capital, what is the maximum credit utilized across the season?
detailed_results.reply: With $60k own capital the capital constraint is binding. The profit-maximizing feasible plan is ~184 ha of soybean (0 corn). Debt peaks just before the soybean sale in f12 (2026-10 H1) at the credit-line limit $100k. If measured after the harvest sale the pre-harvest peak is about $97k in f11. Selling ~266t at harvest to clear the debt and storing the remaining ~490t to 2027-06 gives the highest NPV.

detailed_results.text: On 500 ha with $50,000 capital in Iowa, what is the NPV if supplier terms are 60 days (4 fortnights) with 2% surcharge?
detailed_results.reply: Soy only is optimal under capital. Original feasible soy ~174ha (862$/ha cum). With 4 fortnights delay at 2% you can delay the big inputs f2=171$/ha f6=360$/ha f8=201$/ha to f6/f10/f12, which can be paid from harvest cash in same fortnight. Cash constraint then is f10/f11: 50000-608*X >= -100000 => X~241ha (<250ha rotation limit). Full delay cost = 862*1.02=880$/ha (+~4150$ for 241ha). Harvest 241*4.1=988t @ f12 375.76$/t =371k. After paying f12-f16 delayed costs cash ~221k at f12, ~215k at f29. Discounted at 0.1636%/fortnight (1.0503 for 30f) NPV ~ $200-210k vs ~$163k without trade credit. Storing to f29 404$ -17$ storage earns ~0.7$/t over deposit, +~500$. Partial delay saves ~600$ surcharge.

detailed_results.text: How much does net present value change if capital is $100,000 instead of $50,000 on 500 ha in Iowa?

NPV increase ~$89-90k total; $50k is the extra capital itself, ~$39-40k is extra farming profit. Marginal $1 of own capital returns ~1.80 in NPV, i.e. $0.80 above deposit rate. Optimal is soy-only (corn <50% rule ok, capacity 1000 t), sell just enough at f12 (2026-10) to clear debt (~275 t) and store remainder to f29 (2027-06) - storing all at f12 is only ~$100 less.

Max debt binds at f11. Max feasible soy ~174.9 ha (debt 100k at f11). Debt pre-sale f12 ~$102.7k. Yield 4.1 t/ha = 717 t.
